children: Japan’s S&P Global Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 51.7 in October 2026 from 51.3 in September, but fell short of the flash estimate of 52.0, indicating a modest expansion in activity.
New orders increased at a slightly faster pace, while overseas sales declined at their slowest rate in six months.
Employment continued to grow, though marginally, marking the weakest pace in the 14-month job-creation streak.
Meanwhile, capacity pressures persisted, as unfinished business increased further.
On the price front, both input costs and output charges rose at slower rates, pointing to some easing in inflationary pressures, although inflation remained well above historical trends.
Looking ahead, business confidence fell to its lowest level since March, as concerns over inflation, an ageing population, and persistent labor shortages weighed on the outlook.

title: Japan Services Growth Revised Downward
